messages.author: 6158c2622f0f055d
messages.subject: Anova, MLR estimator
parts:
Hello,

I'm using a MLR estimator for my models, but when I try to compare them with anova(), I get comparisons of ML estimators. Is there any way to get comparisons of MLR estimators?

Thanks!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Anova, MLR estimator
parts:
On 11/19/2016 01:58 PM, nika....@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'm using a MLR estimator for my models, but when I try to compare them
> with anova(), I get comparisons of ML estimators.

No you do not:

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, estimator = "MLR")
fit0 <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, estimator = "MLR",
orthogonal = TRUE)
anova(fit, fit0)

gives

Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (method = "satorra.bentler.2001")

Df AIC BIC Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit 24 7535.5 7646.7 85.305
fit0 27 7597.7 7697.8 153.527 44.625 3 1.112e-09 ***
---
Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Indeed, the Chisq values are the non-scaled versions. But note that
153.527 - 85.305 = 68.222, not 44.625. According to standard theory, it
is the difference of the original chi-square values that are 'rescaled',
not the difference of the scaled chi-square values.

See the references in ?lavtestLRT

Yves.

I have one more question - when I manually subtract the chi-square values that I got with the MLR, I still don't get the same differences.

In my models I get:
model 1: chi-square = 55.764 (24)
model 2: chi-square = 63.197 (30)

When you subtract that you get: chi-square difference = 7.433 (6), while anova gives me: chi-square difference = 8.892 (6).

Is it because of some corrections done in the analysis?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Anova, MLR estimator
parts:
On 11/19/2016 04:43 PM, nika....@gmail.com wrote:
> Thank you very much for your quick reply.
>
> I have one more question - when I manually subtract the chi-square
> values that I got with the MLR, I still don't get the same differences.
>
> In my models I get:
> model 1: chi-square = 55.764 (24)
> model 2: chi-square = 63.197 (30)
>
> When you subtract that you get: chi-square difference = 7.433 (6), while
> anova gives me: chi-square difference = 8.892 (6).
>
> Is it because of some corrections done in the analysis?

Yes. 7.433 is the (naive) chi-square difference; 8.892 is the scaled
(robust) chi-square difference. It is a 'scaled' (or corrected) version
of 7.433

Yves.
